intro.TrustedMarkup:
Typed translations as a generator library.

import { i18n } from "std/i18n"
import { t, setLocale, locale, Locale, TransKey, tCartItems } from i18n("./locales")

i18n(dir) reads every <locale>.json under dir at compile time, checks that the locales agree, compiles each message to a Vyrn function body and returns the module as Code (vyrn emit-gen <file> shows it). The module holds Locale (one variant per file), setLocale/locale, TransKey (the finite type of every dotted key), one function per key with arguments taken from the message and the base-locale message as its doc, t(key), and transKey(s), which checks a runtime String against the key set.

catalogue(dir) reads the same files and writes only one exported function per key and locale, tCartItems__En. It holds no Locale and no module state, so a generator can call it at generation, naming its locale, and two catalogues link in one program, where two En variants would clash.

A message is Unicode MessageFormat 2, read by std/i18n.syntax: text, where a backslash escapes \, {, | and }; a placeholder {$name} (String); .input and .local declarations; and one .match selector with a * variant. :number makes an Int64, selected by an integer key, then by the locale's plural category; :string selects a finite string type of its keys; :list joins an Array<String> as the locale does. Markup, options, attributes and other functions fail generation, as do numbers, booleans and null in a locale file. An argument name may not start with __.

prose.TrustedMarkup: Read every <locale>.json under dir, check the locales, and return the translation module.
Read every <locale>.json under dir, check the locales, and return one exported function per key and locale, each of which reads no module state.
